items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: all I know him by name is Jack Sheen, they call him the Coconut King

ctx.x: What about banjo, how did they tune them in the old days? Everybody used a four string tenor or a spectrum or five string?

Well I can tell you about that. When the banjo, now when they had banjos in the band like I said, they were using the guitar banjo. Because Johnny, not only Johnny's sincere, there was a couple of other guys around there. A fellow named Lorenzo Starr. They used a banjo guitar. In fact like I said before I started playing professional in 24, before the banjo got popular, that's what they were using. And that thing had a pretty good carrying power. Because I remember there was a guy with Sam Morgan band, that was…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: a fellow named, um, Jack Sheen, had opened up the suburban, had built the suburban garden, and we, uh, here, here, at Hyatt Village, the band opened up the place

ctx.x: Well, as I said, we, we, in Pensacola, we were working for these people, and so, uh, we used to play a town like, like Mobile, and go to Montgomery, and, uh, there's a couple other times we'd go. So, uh, around about, uh, let's see, close to 26, well, we left Pensacola, no, we made a trip down to Florida, that's what we made, a trip all over from Pensacola to, uh, Jacksonville, Florida. Well, this guy, here in the...

he was managing the band and booking the band because they didn't have no bookies no day, but he was a man that knew a lot of people, you see. And we booked this all the way to Jacksonville. We stayed, I remember it was in the winter we were in Jacksonville, Florida. And the fella George Morris, he had been a cook one time. He suggested that we go down to Miami or Panama, way down up in there, you see. And well, the fella, they wasn't doing so good on the road and everybody wanted to get back to Pensacola, you…
You missed out the, uh, the Lee Collins period there. Well, I, well, that, oh, yeah, that's right,
